errors.english: this refers to the result of the curd-pot thrown by the hand of (Zhi ba) Shanti falling upon the head
errors.why: བར་དུའོ marks the extent of the cited lemma (the passage runs 'up to' the curd-pot phrase); it is not a gloss explaining what the phrase refers to.

errors.english: because it surpasses the noble ones, it causes beings to progress
errors.why: དམ་པས is instrumental ('being distinguished by excellence it proceeds'); nothing is said about surpassing noble ones or making beings progress.

errors.english: "Complete" means...
errors.why: ཚང here is 'nest', glossed on the next side as 'a dwelling' (གནས་ཡིན་ནོ), not 'complete'.

note: A generally accurate rendering of a lemma-by-lemma Vinaya gloss; a few lemma boundaries and one word misread.

errors.english: The cause of change and the condition of change are also fully known by the Tathagata Thus-Gone One.
errors.why: The sentence continues from the previous side (སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པར་ + འགྱུར་བ): it is the cause and condition of beings' becoming purified, not 'of change'.

fix.find: The cause of change and the condition of change are also fully known by the Tathagata Thus-Gone One.
fix.replace: Whatever is the cause and whatever is the condition of sentient beings' becoming purified, that too is fully known by the Tathagata.

note: Faithful sutra quotation on causes of defilement/purification and the Tathagata's samadhis, except for the misread opening carried over from the previous side.

errors.english: The (vihara) monastic dwelling/temple itself is the builder.
errors.why: བྱེད་པ་པོ་ཉིད here asks what object constitutes (is the locus of) the offence, answered 'the vihara'; it is not a 'builder', which makes the building the agent.

errors.english: If they cover it with wooden planks, there is no offense. If they cover it with shingles, there is no offense.
errors.why: སྤང་ལེབ are turves/sods; ཤིང་ལེབ are the wooden planks, so the two coverings are shifted.

fix.find: If they cover it with wooden planks, there is no offense. If they cover it with shingles, there is no offense.
fix.replace: If they cover it with turves, there is no offense. If they cover it with wooden planks, there is no offense.

note: The argument of this pāyattika commentary is followed correctly; the 'builder' rendering of the technical question and one roofing material are off.

errors.english: are in every way non-existent in nature because they are not perceived in any way
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་ཡང་ renders kathaṃcit 'in some way': the self, pot etc. are in some respect non-existent because in some respect not perceived (the Jaina-style example), not 'in every way'.

fix.find: are in every way non-existent in nature because they are not perceived in any way
fix.replace: are in some way non-existent in nature because they are in some way not perceived

errors.english: are in every way existent in nature because they are perceived in whatever way
errors.why: Again kathaṃcit: a hare's horn etc. are in some way existent because in some way perceived; 'in every way existent' says something the text does not.

fix.find: are in every way existent in nature because they are perceived in whatever way
fix.replace: are in some way existent in nature because they are in some way perceived

errors.english: it does not function because of certainty
errors.why: The reason, though it has the three marks, does not operate to produce certainty; certainty is what is lacking, not what blocks it.

fix.find: it does not function because of certainty
fix.replace: it does not serve to produce certainty

errors.english: exist independently
errors.why: The verse says the invariable connection never resides in the three modes; the English adds 'independently' and makes the three modes the subject.

errors.english: This is the second characteristic.
errors.why: Parallel to མཚན་ཉིད་གཅིག་པ 'having a single characteristic', this is a reason 'having two characteristics' (the moon has no similar instance), not 'the second characteristic'.

errors.english: Whether a thing is an entity or a non-entity, it is perceived as having its own identity in whatever way it may be.
errors.why: This is an example inference: an entity or non-entity is of existent nature, because it is in some way perceived; thesis and reason are merged into one statement.

note: Pātrasvāmin's verses against the triple mark are followed in outline, but the kathaṃcit examples, the 'two-characteristic' reason and the certainty clause are mistranslated.

errors.english: the lord of the immortals [note: Indra, king of the gods] and the teacher of the gods
errors.why: The compound most likely names one figure, the guru of the lord of the immortals (Bṛhaspati, Indra's preceptor), to whom the king is likened, not Indra and Bṛhaspati as two.

note: A good literary rendering of the end of the Ṛṣi jātaka and the opening of the next story.

span_why: The opening 'If one asks, "Then what is it?", it is from the object.' translates a sentence from the previous side, before the sentence that crosses the boundary.

errors.english: At that time, the mental engagement with a lamp would also become that.
errors.why: The lamp and attention (manaskāra) are two further causes that would also have to be remembered there, as the commentary on light and attention shows; not 'attention to a lamp'.

fix.find: At that time, the mental engagement with a lamp would also become that.
fix.replace: At that time, the lamp and mental engagement would also be [remembered] there.

errors.english: so too would appearance become
errors.why: སྣང་བ here is light (āloka), the lamp of the verse, as a cause of cognition, not 'appearance'.

errors.english: Because cognition and memory are the results of the object,
errors.why: ཤེས་དྲན is 'the memory of the cognition' (because the cognition is an effect of the object), not cognition and memory as two results.

note: The anti-anākāra argument about memory is mostly followed, but the root verse on lamp and attention is misconstrued and the start carries in text from the previous side.

errors.english: the Madhyamaka Middle Way school that advocates for cessation
errors.why: འགོག་པ here is negation/refutation (a 'Madhyamaka of negation'), not cessation (nirodha).

note: A sound translation of the defence of the Mahāyāna as Buddha-word, including the patriarch lineage.
A careful, faithful rendering of a difficult passage on qualifying the statement of similarity and the general rule versus exception.

errors.english: The definition of the state of the general principal
errors.why: The side opens by concluding that pradhāna is therefore not wholly unseen, and that if this is held it contradicts the verse 'The guṇas…'; this is not translated.

fix.find: The definition of the state of the general principal
fix.replace: …is manifest. Therefore it is not that it is never seen. If that is what you hold, then this here is contradictory. If you wonder what it contradicts: "The guṇas" and so on. The definition of the state of the general principal

errors.english: However, the capacity, which is of a non-hollow nature, is entirely different from the manifest state
errors.why: This is the Sāṃkhya opponent's second alternative (introduced as an anticipated doubt on the next side), presented in the English as the author's own conclusion.

note: The critique of pradhāna as 'hollow' is mostly followed, but the opening lines are dropped and the opponent's rejoinder is not marked as such.

errors.english: It describes the kinds of Buddha-fields present in those Bodhisattvas
errors.why: The text says what kind of bodhisattvas appeared in the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas; the English inverts fields and bodhisattvas.

fix.find: It describes the kinds of Buddha-fields present in those Bodhisattvas
fix.replace: It describes what kind of Bodhisattvas there were in the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas

errors.english: dimensions, waters, and circumferences
errors.why: ཞེང and ཆུ are breadth and length (cf. ཆུ་ཞེང), with circumference; ཆུ is not 'waters'.

note: The list of past deeds shown in one body is broadly conveyed, but the field dimensions and the bodhisattvas-in-fields clause are mistranslated.
